name: Security Incidents
blurb: Major AI security events as they are disclosed.

reading.body:
Lambda accounts for a disproportionate share of active AI security incidents in this dataset, recording open incidents in 62 of 97 observed periods and reaching a peak of 3 concurrent open incidents, more than any other tracked provider.

The daily series shows a cluster of elevated activity between August 14 and August 24, with counts ranging from 2 to 4 incidents per day before dropping sharply toward the end of August and into September. That pattern is consistent with either a single prolonged event generating multiple disclosures or a short wave of distinct incidents across providers. The data does not distinguish between those possibilities, and it does not describe the nature, severity, or affected systems behind any individual incident.

Six providers are named in the per-provider breakdown out of 12 total tracked, so the table is partial. Among those named, OpenAI shows the next highest incident-bearing observation count at 12, while ElevenLabs and Baseten each show 3, suggesting meaningful dispersion in incident frequency across the ecosystem. What the data cannot say is whether incidents at compute-intensive inference providers carry different downstream consequences than those at application-layer providers, even though that distinction matters for understanding risk to the broader AI supply chain.
